messages:
sanjay: Hey team, new here. Using macOS Monterey on an M2. Trying to standardize runtimes with asdf (nodejs, python, ruby). Followed the onboarding doc but my `python3` keeps resolving to /usr/bin/python3 instead of ~/.asdf/shims/python. asdf reshim didn't help. Also npm global installs are landing under /usr/local/bin and clobbering yarn binary versions. Anyone seen shim precedence problems on ARM macs?
olivia: Welcome! Common culprits: your shell startup order might export PATH with /usr/local/bin before ~/.asdf/shims. What shell are you using? zsh? fish?
sanjay: zsh (oh-my-zsh). My .zshrc sources dotfiles that set PATH early. I tried `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH"` but still weird.
maria: For zsh with omz, make sure asdf init runs after omz so the shims are first. Typical snippet in ~/.zshrc: 

  # after oh-my-zsh init
  source $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh
  export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH"

Also check `which -a python3` to see the lookup order.
sanjay: `which -a python3` shows: /usr/bin/python3 then ~/.asdf/shims/python3 then /opt/homebrew/bin/python3. So why is asdf shim second?
ben: Could be that your PATH contains /usr/bin earlier because of login vs interactive shell differences. Check `echo $PATH` inside the terminal you use (and inside VS Code terminal). VS Code sometimes launches login shells differently.
infra-bot: Note: internal onboarding checklist item OG-89 recommends adding `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"` to the top of interactive shell rc for macs.
olivia: Also confirm that `asdf which python3` returns the shim path. If the shim exists but is not first, run `hash -r` (zsh) or restart the shell to flush cached paths.
sanjay: Ran `hash -r` and restarted, but still prefer system python. I realized my dotfiles set `PATH` earlier via a helper `dotpath()` function and then source oh-my-zsh. So moving asdf init after that made it first.
maria: About npm globals: on Apple Silicon, Homebrew defaults to /opt/homebrew, but some older instructions still add /usr/local. Check `npm config get prefix`. If it's /usr/local, change to your asdf/node global dir: `npm config set prefix $HOME/.asdf/installs/nodejs/$(asdf current nodejs)/lib` or use `corepack`/pnpm/nvm style tools. We usually avoid global installs by using `npx` or project-local binstubs.
sanjay: `npm config get prefix` was /usr/local. I changed it to `~/.asdf/installs/nodejs/18.17.1/.npm-global` and added that to PATH. Globals now land in ~/.npm-global/bin and don't clobber /opt/homebrew.
ben: If you use VS Code devcontainers, add a `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` `remoteUser` and ensure PATH in container is set. Host-side PATH changes don't affect container unless you pass env.
sanjay: Thanks! Final gotcha: python venvs were created by system python when I ran `python3 -m venv .venv` before asdf was first in PATH. Had to delete and recreate venv after fixing PATH.
maria: Yep. Also consider adding a small checklist to your onboarding PR: asdf init after omz, set npm prefix to home npm-global, verify `which -a` & `echo $PATH`. I'll open a tiny docs PR.
infra-bot: Created ticket IT-4520: "New-hire checklist: ensure asdf init ordering and npm prefix guidance" assigned to maria.
sanjay: Very helpful, appreciate the quick responses :thumbsup:
